newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: China executes five Uighur riot leaders - exiles.
newsitem.headline: China executes five Uighur riot leaders - exiles.

text.p: A Uighur exile group said on Monday China had executed five ethnic Uighurs who were accused of involvement in bloody riots that rocked the country's predominantly Moslem northwest province of Xinjiang last month.

"We know for sure that five people (Uighurs) were executed on March 20 (Thursday)," Mukhiddin Mukhlisi, spokesman for the United National Revolutionary Front of East Turkestan, told Reuters at a congress of exile Uighur groups near Kazakhstan's capital Almaty.

Officials in Xinjiang said last week they had indicted six people, who could face the death penalty if convicted, in connection with anti-Chinese rioting in the province. But they denied allegations made by exiled Uighur separatists that China would execute two rioters.
Mukhlisi said the executions took place in the town of Yining, located near the China-Kazakh border and scene of last month's disturbances which left nine dead and 198 wounded.

Mukhlisi named one of those executed as Abdukhalil Abdulmedchit, saying he was a prominent leader in the rioting, but he could not name the other four. He said the two names he gave last week of two students facing execution were incorrect.
Information from the remote, closed region of mountain and desert is difficult to verify. News often arrives days late via traders crossing the China-Kazakh border.
